title: Dishonored Was A Last Ditch Effort By Arkane Studios After Years Of Fruitless Contract Work According To The Games Co Creator I Think We Had Four Months Of Money Left
report:
The best immersive sims are a beloved and dedicated bunch. Their worlds can be complex, their lore deep. Their fans expect nothing less than a certain level of quality in sequels.

ZeniMax Media's acquisition of id Software was one such example. Following the release of Dishonored 2, it became clear that Arkane Studios' new parent company wasn't going to allow them to work on a third instalment.

"We were about to get into a third part of something," says Smith. "We had been doing this for six years. We done two games. Now they are telling us 'you can't do a third game.' That was one we really needed, because we didn't want to make another Dishonored."

However, the development of another immersive sim is possible thanks to an new partnership with Private Division, which will allow Arkane to release their own IP for PC and console. The deal comes as a result of a long-term strategy from Smith, who started making plans following the ZeniMax acquisition.

"We need to do what we're passionate about," he says. "The best way you can be is just make a game that you really like and hope people will get it."

Arkane's latest project is a prime example of this strategy in action. The company has been working on Redfall, the first mainline Dishonored sequel, which was teased earlier this year.

Despite some delays, Smith has promised "big changes" to the immersive sim series with its next instalment, which is expected to launch later than previously announced.

title: 7 Greatest Far Side Comics With No Words

The article showcases seven of Larson's comic strips that feature no words at all, including a penguin slipping on a banana peel on ice, flies forming a firing squad, and other humorous scenarios.
